author: Rahul kp
title: Leverage:
simple_words: Leverage shows how much a small change in sales shakes EBIT and EPS, because of fixed costs.

definitions.meaning: Effect of fixed operating cost: a % change in sales gives a larger % change in EBIT.
definitions.note: No fixed cost and EBIT positive: DOL = 1

definitions.meaning: Effect of fixed financing cost (interest, preference dividend): a % change in EBIT gives a larger % change in EPS.
definitions.note: No interest or pref. dividend: DFL = 1

key_points: ==DOL== works on the business risk side: Sales to EBIT.
==DFL== works on the financial risk side: EBIT to EPS.
!!DOL is 1 or more only when EBIT is positive (above break-even)!!.

formulas.name: Degree of Operating Leverage
formulas.legend: Contribution = Sales − Variable cost. EBIT = Contribution − Fixed operating cost. Valid when EBIT is not zero.

formulas.name: Degree of Financial Leverage
formulas.legend: EBT = EBIT − Interest. t = tax rate. Without preference dividend, denominator is just EBT.

formulas.name: Degree of Combined Leverage
formulas.legend: DCL = DOL × DFL. If preference dividend exists, denominator is EBT − Pref. div/(1−t), same as in DFL.

insight.text: Higher fixed operating or financing cost means higher DOL or DFL, so higher risk and higher reward.

memory_trick.explanation: DOL and DFL each divide a P&L line by the line just below it. DCL divides Contribution by EBT, which skips EBIT.

steps: Write the P&L down to EPS
exam_tip: Check the question's wording: if it asks for DCL, Contribution/EBT and DOL × DFL must give the same answer.

doubt.question: Can DOL be negative?
doubt.answer: Yes. Below break-even, EBIT is negative, so DOL is negative. At break-even EBIT is zero and DOL is undefined.

mistakes.right: DOL = Contribution / EBIT. When EBIT is positive, it is 1 if no fixed cost, more than 1 if there is fixed cost.

mistakes.wrong: Using EBIT in the denominator of DCL
mistakes.right: DCL = Contribution / EBT, or DOL × DFL.
Deduct Pref. dividend/(1 − t) from EBT in the denominator.

mistakes.wrong: Adding DOL and DFL to get DCL
mistakes.right: DCL = DOL × DFL, not DOL + DFL.

reviewer_note: Definition note and mistake 1 now state the positive-EBIT condition. Check that DFL/DCL pref dividend grossed-up treatment matches the ICAI study material.
check_notes: Writer: Definition note and mistake 1 now state the positive-EBIT condition. Check that DFL/DCL pref dividend grossed-up treatment matches the ICAI study material.

Checker 1: Step 4 ('Apply DFL = EBIT/EBT') leaves out preference dividend, which contradicts formula 2 and mistake 3. It should read: 'Apply DFL = EBIT / [EBT − Pref. div/(1−t)]; this is just EBIT/EBT when there is no preference dividend.'

Checker 1: Doubt answer: DOL is negative below break-even only while contribution is still positive (sales above variable cost). Suggested wording: 'Yes. Below break-even (contribution positive, EBIT negative), DOL is negative. At break-even, EBIT is zero and DOL is undefined.'
